term: International Society for Music Information Retrieval
definition: The International Society for Music Information Retrieval (ISMIR) is an international forum for research on the organization of music-related data.
details: It started as an informal group steered by an ad hoc committee in 2000 which established a yearly symposium - whence "ISMIR", which meant International Symposium on Music Information Retrieval. It was turned into a conference in 2002 while retaining the acronym. ISMIR was incorporated in Canada on July 4, 2008.

explainer.lead: ISMIR is an international forum for research on organizing music-related data, incorporated in Canada on 4 July 2008. It matters because it anchors a research community around music data analysis and retrieval.

tiers.eli5: It is like a club for people who study how computers can sort, search, and understand music.
tiers.practitioner: Music-information researchers target its yearly conference to present work on music data organization. A pitfall is confusing the society with its conference, since the acronym originally meant symposium and was kept when it became a conference in 2002.
tiers.paperLevel: It began as an informal group steered by an ad hoc committee in 2000 that established a yearly symposium; it became a conference in 2002, kept the ISMIR acronym, and was incorporated in Canada on 4 July 2008. Limits: it is a society and conference, not a standards body.

explainer.example: A team studying music tagging submits to the ISMIR conference, which grew from the 2000 symposium and the 2002 conference.
